subject: SwiftBoard discovery: performance envelope & token ceiling ops
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma@swiftboard.ai>, Carlos Mendez <carlos@swiftboard.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-11T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: SwiftBoard discovery — initial perf clarifying questions

Thanks again for the call today — good to meet the team. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can size a focused perf qualification POC: 

Summary (from call)
- Primary latency target: you mentioned wanting sub-400ms p95 for the suggestion flows; confirm if 350ms p95 is the hard target or a goal.
- Peak throughput: you said ~100-150 reqs/s for launch.
- Typical concurrency per tenant: ~30-50 concurrent users, but bursty during syncs.
- Streaming: you said some UX components need early partial tokens (type-ahead) while other flows are batch generation.
- Token envelope: most calls are "input-heavy" (context + user history). Need clarified max input/output tokens.

Questions for us to qualify perf SLOs:
1) Can you share a small sample of representative payload sizes (input tokens distribution and expected output lengths)?
2) Are the type-ahead flows strict hard-latency (e.g., 150-250ms) or acceptable as lower-priority streaming?
3) Do you require per-request routing to a pinned model (for determinism) or are fallbacks acceptable?
4) Any networking constraints (on-prem connectors, extra egress hops) we should account for?

Proposed next steps
- If you share a 100-sample token histogram we can propose an SLO matrix and a canary plan (client-side harness + server-side telemetry).
- We’ll put together two candidate profiles: low-latency (reserved pool, aggressive batching/kv cache) and high-throughput (cheaper model, higher p95) with explicit token ceilings and fallbacks.

Attachments referenced: rough_perf_matrix.xlsx (draft sizing), redwood_slo_playbook.pdf (examples).

Thanks — I’ll loop Marissa for the tech runbook and a tentative test harness link.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.com

From: Emma Liu <emma@swiftboard.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos@swiftboard.ai>
Date: 2025-10-11T18:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SwiftBoard discovery — initial perf clarifying questions

Hi Priyom — thanks for the clear notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: our goal for the type-ahead UX is p95 <= 350ms end-to-end. Non-interactive batch generation (reporting) can tolerate up to 1.2s p95.
- Throughput: plan for 120 reqs/s sustained with 2x burst capacity during peak imports (~240 reqs/s).
- Concurrency: 40 concurrent active request streams per tenant is a safe planning number.
- Streaming: yes, type-ahead needs streaming for partial responses; it can be prioritized over other flows.
- Token sizes: typical input ~1.2k tokens; heavy-context flows (chat transcripts) can be up to 8k tokens occasionally. Output is usually 150–800 tokens depending on flow.

We can share a 200-sample set of payloads (anonymized) by end of day Friday. Regarding pinned models — prefer deterministic pinned models for the suggestion flow to avoid regressions during rollout. Fallbacks acceptable for non-critical paths.

Attachments: sample_payloads.zip (I’ll upload to the Drive link you give).

— Emma
Emma Liu
VP Product, SwiftBoard
emma@swiftboard.ai

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma@swiftboard.ai>, Carlos Mendez <carlos@swiftboard.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-12T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SwiftBoard discovery — initial perf clarifying questions

Appreciate the details — this helps a lot. High-level plan and tradeoffs below so we can align on an SLO matrix for the POC.

High-level recommendation (two-profile approach)
- Profile A — Low-latency suggestion flow (p95 <= 350ms):
  * Model: Redwood-Lite-4Q (quantized) or equivalent low-latency variant
  * Deployment: reserved tenant pool (dedicated capacity) to reduce cold start and noisy neighbor variability
  * Batching: small-batch aggressive KV prefix caching for common prompts
  * Streaming: enabled, prioritized queueing (circuit-breaker if queue depth > X)
  * Token ceiling: recommend hard input cap at 6k tokens for this profile; for >6k route to Profile B or a chunked fallback.

- Profile B — High-throughput / heavy-context (p95 target <= 1.2s):
  * Model: Redwood-Standard or open variant with larger context support
  * Deployment: burstable shared pool with autoscale; cheaper quantization options allowable
  * Token ceiling: allow up to 12k inputs with longer tail latency; implement prefix pruning to reduce cost

Tradeoffs / notes
- Streaming adds complexity to KV cache and increases token accounting; partial responses still count against billing and influence latency budgeting.
- If deterministic pinned model is required for suggestions, we recommend a canary rollout window for 48–72 hours with fidelity checks against a baseline prompt set.
- For bursts, recommend a staged fallback: reserved pool -> burstable pool -> reduced-output fallback (truncate context / synthesize) to keep latency predictable.

Action items for SwiftBoard to accelerate sizing
1) Share the 200-sample payloads (tokenized) and indicate which flows require streaming vs batch.
2) Give us an expected concurrency curve (per-minute) for your peak events.
3) Confirm whether pinned-model determinism is required for all tenants or only a rollout subset.

I’ve attached a draft SLO playbook and a rough perf matrix (see attachments). Marissa — can you propose a canary runbook (test harness details + telemetry points) we can share with SwiftBoard?

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma@swiftboard.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-13T11:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SwiftBoard discovery — initial perf clarifying questions

Thanks — looping in engineering runbook items. Proposed immediate next steps and tentative dates: 

1) Test harness + sample upload
   - I’ll create a Drive folder and drop a simple harness (k6 + tokenized payloads) by COB today. Expect link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XswExampleDriveLink
2) Canary plan
   - Canary window: 48 hours (can extend to 72 if we see instability)
   - Telemetry: per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), token counts (input/output), backend GPU utilization, queue depth, KV cache hit rate
3) Acceptance criteria (initial)
   - Profile A: p95 <= 350ms for 90% of canary traffic, no more than 5% error rate
   - Profile B: p95 <= 1.2s with throughput sustain >= 85% of target
4) Meeting to kickoff: propose Thursday 2025-10-15 11:00 AM PT — 30 minutes to walk the harness and roles.

Action items assigned:
- Emma: upload the 200-sample payloads to the drive and flag streaming flows.
- Carlos: provide concurrency curve for peak import.
- Priyom: share SLO matrix and short model recommendation table.
- Ben: readiness check for a reserved pool quote (capacity sizing).

I’ll attach the canary_runbook.md and a quick perf checklist.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
